worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\frac{6x-11}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-4}+\frac{B}{(x-4)^{2}}.
$$

Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-4)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-11 & =A(x-4)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=4$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6(4)-11 & =A(4-4)+B \\ 13 & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $B$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6(0)-11 & =A(0-4)+13 \\ -11 & =-4A+13 \\ -4A & =-24 \\ A & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\frac{6x-11}{(x-4)^{2}}=\frac{6}{x-4}+\frac{13}{(x-4)^{2}}.
$$
